The core innovation lies in combining Bayesian model choice with variable selection through RJ-MCMC, enabling simultaneous inference over both structure (PO vs NPO) and inclusion (variable selection). The cumulative link model defines the likelihood function, while stochastic ordering enforces logical consistency. The RJ-MCMC explores the model space by proposing moves that switch between PO and NPO structures per variable, maintaining validity through bounded proposal regions. This dual capability allows GSE to dynamically adjust its ordinal outcome models based on empirical evidence, optimizing for both fit and interpretability. Failure modes include computational inefficiency from high-dimensional model space and potential violation of stochastic ordering outside observed ranges. The method's strength lies in its ability to produce model-averaged predictions that reflect uncertainty in both structure and inclusion, making it suitable for GSI’s probabilistic inference tasks.
